current_bottleneck: 333a's masked full-path objective is alive but under-coupled. It learns path-level calibration and cointegration better than many one-shot flows, but IID future source tokens plus local axial mixing do not create enough common-shock geometry or regime-responsive width.
last_result_summary: Postmortem after 333a: the useful move is not more capacity or temperature. The full-path objective improved aggregate coverage, daily KS, median bias, and cointegration, while the failures concentrate in common-shock coupling, per-cell coverage balance, regime width, and pathwise max-jump shape.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 333b as the single clean repair: keep the same masked full-path rectified-flow objective and standardized-logit coordinate, but add a generic global scenario mixer inside each axial block by pooling hidden states over the full time-cell grid and broadcasting the learned global state back. Falsifier: improve cross-cell corr/rank, regime width, and per-cell tails without losing 333a's coverage/cointegration gains.
current_best_note: 330a and 330c tie the 5/11 frontier with cleaner first-principles autoregressive sequence-density models, without retrieval, low-rank readouts, residual shells, or evaluator-specific losses.
